findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in cleartext in the Lambda function's environment variables, committed to source control. Anyone with read access to the repo, the Lambda configuration, or lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration can retrieve these long-lived credentials.

No kms_key_arn is specified, so the environment variables (which contain secrets) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key, without customer-managed key control or the additional client-side encryption helpers. Sensitive values are therefore visible in plaintext in the console and API to any principal with basic Lambda read permissions.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which has reached end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the execution environment unremediated.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function runs outside any VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or subnet boundary. Combined with the embedded static credentials, this eases exfiltration if the function is compromised.

The trust policy allows lambda.amazonaws.com to assume the role with no aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn condition, so the role is not scoped to a specific function or account, widening the confused-deputy attack surface.
